chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And mention Allah during the numbered days.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'These are the days of Al-Tashreeq. When they stayed in Mina after the sacrifice, they would boast, and one of them would say, 'My father used to do such and such.'
So Allah, Majestic is His Praise, said: 'Then when you depart from Arafat, mention Allah as you mentioned your fathers, or with a greater mention.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the Takbeer is: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. Allah is the Greatest. And for Allah is the Praise. Allah is the Greatest upon what He has guided us. Allah is the Greatest upon what He has graced us with from the beasts of the livestock.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of Al-Tashreeq (11th-13th Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.عَرَفاتٍ: Arafat (the plain where pilgrims stand during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific formula for Takbeer during the Days of Al-Tashreeq according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi elucidates the 'numbered days' of Surah Al-Baqarah as the Days of Tashreeq, highlighting a shift from the pre-Islamic practice of ancestral boasting to a superior, divine remembrance. It prescribes the specific liturgical formula for Takbeer, emphasizing gratitude for guidance and sustenance, which underscores the Shia emphasis on ritual precision and spiritual introspection during the Hajj season.
